clue.text: Superagent a long time in captivity

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional superagent 007
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A secret agent spends a long spell held prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage is a state of servitude or being held captive.

clue.text: A trade union address that smacks of the monastery

explanation.surface: A form of words used between trade unionists that sounds rather monkish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade unionists traditionally hail each other by this fraternal title, and it is also the title of a monk.

clue.text: One-eyed teases

explanation.surface: A one-eyed person is mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing pins with a single eye are this word as a noun; as a verb it means provokes or taunts.

clue.text: Top accommodation often reserved for the lowly

definitions.text: Top accommodation often reserved for the lowly

parts.words: Top accommodation often reserved for the lowly
parts.note: top suggests the best, but here it is the room at the top of the house, traditionally given to servants and poor lodgers

explanation.surface: The best rooms are often kept for humble people.
explanation.definitionFit: The room under the roof, highest in a house, was where servants or poor tenants lived.

clue.text: I vex Poles into highly charged state

indicators.note: the letters of these words are worked into a new form, the state that follows

explanation.surface: Someone annoys Polish people until tempers flare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into ... state' signals the anagram of I VEX POLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something likely to blow up, physically or emotionally, is volatile and highly charged.

clue.text: Place in the sun? Could be an awkward situation

explanation.surface: A sunny place might turn out to be trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny resort is a hot place in a literal sense; idiomatically the phrase means a dangerous or difficult position.

clue.text: A race within inhumane limits

indicators.note: within the limits of the word inhumane, so the answer is held inside it

explanation.surface: A race carried out under cruel restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within ... limits' tells you the answer sits inside 'inhumane'. 'A race' is the definition: mankind is called the human race.
explanation.definitionFit: Mankind is described as a race of beings, the species of people.

clue.text: Thatcher's advice to countrymen asking the way?

definitions.text: Thatcher's advice to countrymen asking the way?

parts.words: Thatcher's advice to countrymen asking the way?
parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, the right-wing British prime minister, would naturally give directions toward the political right

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher directs lost rural folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was a Conservative British prime minister; the direction she would recommend is also a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving direction to go clockwise at a junction doubles as a call to move politically conservative.

clue.text: Pa swished a cane as a cure for everything

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters are swished around, rearranged as a cane is swung

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Father swung a stick as his remedy for all ills.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal remedy, a cure-all, is the classical term for a medicine that heals every disease.

clue.text: It may rage in a stream or in a river

definitions.text: It may rage in a stream

indicators.note: the second in places the word or inside the river named

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that may surge either along a brook or a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' (the second one) puts OR inside TRENT, a long river in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rush of water in a channel is a raging flow.

clue.text: Surpass with openwork

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: To outdo someone using lacy, perforated craftwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openwork' looks like one word for lace, but it splits into 'open' and 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise above or exceed something is to top it, go beyond it.

clue.text: Navigator of Flat Earth, perhaps, getting jittery near rim!

indicators.note: jittery letters move nervously out of place, giving a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A sailor on a flat world grows nervous near its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman or sailor steers ships; one on a flat world would fear the rim.

clue.text: Old currency for a divided monarchy

parts.note: something divided in two is in halves
the crown stands for the monarchy

explanation.surface: Old money suitable for a kingdom split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: A HALF-CROWN was a pre-decimal British coin worth two shillings and sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: This pre-1971 British coin, worth an eighth of a pound, is an old form of money.

clue.text: Made in Peru, cheap frilling

indicators.note: a product made in somewhere is inside it, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: Cheap frills manufactured in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered strip of fabric used to trim a garment is a frill.

clue.text: Newly risen sap product useful for plastics

indicators.note: newly suggests the word risen is made anew, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh sap that has come up from a tree is useful to industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky substance from tree sap, and synthetic versions of it, are the raw stuff of many plastics.

clue.text: How the pre-Raphaelites painted, of course

explanation.surface: A comment on the Victorian painters' style.
explanation.definitionFit: The pre-Raphaelites aimed to paint true to nature; the word also means certainly, as expected.

clue.text: I'm going to and fro to admit a settler

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word is taken there and back, once forwards and once backwards

parts.note: the same word read the other way
to grant is to concede or admit

explanation.surface: Someone travels back and forth to let a settler in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to and fro' gives I'M forwards then backwards, IM then MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes to live permanently in a new country settles there.

clue.text: Parisian underground dwarf sounds a good timekeeper

parts.note: the Paris subway system is the Metro

indicators.note: the word for the dwarf is said aloud, its silent g dropping out

parts.note: a gnome is a dwarfish figure of folklore

explanation.surface: A small creature living in the Paris subway makes a reliable clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that ticks a steady beat keeps time for musicians.

clue.text: Reverse the menu order to get this confection

definitions.text: Reverse the menu order to get this confection

parts.words: Reverse the menu order to get this confection
parts.note: a menu serves the main course before the dessert; swap those two words and you name a confection

explanation.surface: A diner swaps the courses to end up with a candy.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a candy or sugared delicacy is a confection.

clue.text: Had a try with a knife

definitions.text: Had a try with a knife

parts.words: Had a try with a knife
parts.note: to have a go is to have a stab, and with a knife that becomes literal

explanation.surface: Someone attempted something using a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab is to attempt; a knife thrust makes the idiom literal.

clue.text: Unending note; bird a beginner!

parts.note: E is a musical note
a tern is a seabird
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A never-ending note from a novice bird.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no end.

clue.text: How one might drink to a Scot without company

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without signals that company is taken out of the word Scot

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a lone Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes CO (company) from SCOT, leaving ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking in someone's honour is to raise a glass to them.

clue.text: How the last horse ran in the flat at Rotherham?

indicators.note: in tells you the answer is concealed inside these words

explanation.surface: A slow horse trails home in a flat race at a Yorkshire course.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotherham is a town in Yorkshire; the flat is flat racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse at a gentle pace between walk and canter comes in last.

clue.text: With which the meticulous bookkeeper shows good balance

definitions.text: With which the meticulous bookkeeper shows good balance

parts.words: With which the meticulous bookkeeper shows good balance
parts.note: a neat accountant's healthy balance is a large amount of money, and also a sum written neatly

explanation.surface: A careful accountant produces a healthy balance.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerable amount of money is called this idiom, and a careful bookkeeper's figures are orderly.

clue.text: Mohammedan prince, raised in Bow, answers roll-call

indicators.note: brought up in Bow, in Cockney East London, so the words are said with a dropped h

parts.note: on a roll-call one answers 'me, here'

explanation.surface: An Eastern prince brought up in London's East End responds to a register.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in the East End of London, where Cockneys drop the h, so 'here' is said 'ere.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir or ruler in Muslim lands is a title variously spelt.

clue.text: But 11 couldn't buy half such a royal estate

definitions.text: But 11 couldn't buy half such a royal estate

parts.words: But 11 couldn't buy half such a royal estate
parts.note: the coin at 11 across is only half of a crown, the first word of this royal property

explanation.surface: An old coin was too little to buy even part of a monarch's land.
explanation.definitionFit: Property owned by the sovereign is the monarch's estate.

clue.text: A sort of oven-ready baking apple?

definitions.text: A sort of oven-ready baking apple?

parts.words: A sort of oven-ready baking apple?
parts.note: a baking apple is prepared by removing its middle before going in the oven

explanation.surface: A kind of apple ready for baking.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple with its middle taken out is prepared for baking.

clue.text: Fresher in tune we recorded

indicators.note: in shows the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: We recorded a tune that sounds more modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more recent is fresher.

clue.text: He makes a hash of ram's head, leg and bun

indicators.note: a hash is a jumble, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook ruins a dish of mutton, leg and bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ram's head' gives R; 'makes a hash of' scrambles R, LEG and BUN.
explanation.definitionFit: He refers to the man who botches things, a clumsy person.

clue.text: How the student nurse advances her career

definitions.text: How the student nurse advances her career

parts.words: How the student nurse advances her career
parts.note: a trainee nurse progresses by working in the hospital rooms where patients lie

explanation.surface: A trainee nurse moves forward in her profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving forward is going ahead, and a nurse works in hospital rooms for patients.

clue.text: Held up the non-clerical element in the act

indicators.note: in places the non-clerical part within the word for an act

parts.note: a deed is an act
lay means not of the clergy

explanation.surface: A clergyman stopped by laypeople in mid-ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held up is being late or postponed.

clue.text: A mistake to set rare mince before small stomach!

indicators.note: the letters of the word are set in a new order, as with mince

parts.note: tum is a child's word for stomach, a little one

explanation.surface: Advice to serve rare minced meat to a little belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' and 'mince' both signal the anagram of RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing slip listed for correction is an error.
